dt-example.title: Hash location (id matching)
dt-example.info:
We've seen in the [previous](./searchId) [two examples](./searchName) how a query parameter can be used to for state loading on initialisation. It is also possible to use a hash location. This is typically used for linking to a specific part of a document though [an anchor tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/a), making it ideal for bookmarking states as well.
To use a hash for state bookmarking, set `-init stateRestore.bookmark.src` to be simply `#`. The id (or name if configured) of the state is the part that follows. Updating our examples, we now have:
* [Search - London](./hashId#1) * [Order - Position](./hashId#2) * [Search and order](./hashId#3)
Again, click the links to reload the page with the selected state active. Note that in this case the page does not do a full reload, since the hash does not trigger that behaviour in the browser. Instead, StateRestore has a listener to take effect, so it will load the state on initial load, or as the end user clicks links for the page.
Next: [Hash location and state name matching](./hashName).
